prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: one transparent PNG MIDGE SWARM miniature on a shared round tabletop base, for 48/64/96px RPG display.
Primary request: replace all three bees in Image 1 with a clearly different group of MIDGES. Image 1 is the style/base edit target: keep its high downward three-quarter camera, soft upper-left light, matte hand-painted miniature finish and neutral dark grey-brown thin circular disc with subdued bronze-grey bevel. Image 2 is the native midge-swarm identity reference, a dense mass of tiny dark flying insects. Translate that identity into a legible sculpted group; do not reproduce pixel noise.
Subject and layout: exactly SEVEN complete small midges, similar in size, arranged as a loose irregular C-shaped ascending swarm across the disc, with an obvious open centre and a few separate insects to either side. Their bodies face varied directions; the group reads as a restless airy swarm, not a three-bee triangle, neat radial emblem or symmetric bouquet. Spread the seven insects enough to keep their bodies and wings identifiable, with visible base gaps between them. All insects belong to one asset on one base.
Midge anatomy: slender dark grey-brown elongated bodies, small rounded thorax, narrow tapering abdomen, six fine bent legs, small natural insect heads with antennae, and ONE PAIR of narrow pale smoky-silver translucent wings per insect. Bodies are long and thin rather than barrel-shaped; no fluffy yellow thorax, no yellow-black bee stripes, no pinched wasp waist, no large hornet stinger. Each insect must remain a coherent insect, not detached dots, extra wings or disconnected legs. Slightly emphasize thorax and wing planes so the silhouettes remain readable at small size, while keeping them delicate compared with the bee reference.
Value and family distinction: the overall group is sparse dark slender bodies threaded through many light narrow wing planes; much more negative space and a lighter, finer density than the three large plump yellow bee miniatures. Broad smoke-grey wings and selective thorax planes must separate dark bodies from the disc in grayscale, without luminous outlines. No opaque haze, painted motion cloud or scattered noise.
Shared framing: square 1024x1024 canvas; centred almost-circular thin disc around 86% of canvas width, matching Image 1. The complete swarm spans about 80% of disc diameter. Every wing, antenna and leg stays inside the disc with a visible perimeter strip. Keep the main recognisable insects away from the top-right 23% by 18% canvas badge area; no mark or guide is drawn.
Style: painted carved/resin tabletop miniatures, coherent simplified anatomy and broad small wing planes, matte finish, soft upper-left illumination, tiny subdued shadows only on the disc. Insects may hover just above the surface but no stands, rods, terrain or outside shadow.
Backdrop: genuine native transparent alpha outside the base, clean antialiased perimeter.
Avoid: bees, wasps, butterflies, fluffy yellow bodies, stripes, flowers, scenery, fog, faction rings, coloured rim, crowns, rank, HP, shields, selection, text, numbers, icons, watermark, black/white backdrop and painted checkerboard. One swarm on one neutral disc; no contact sheet.
reference_roles: Style/base edit target and negative family contrast; retain disc/paint/light/camera but replace all large striped bees and triangular layout.
Native midge swarm identity reference; dark tiny flying swarm, interpreted as readable slender midge miniatures.
authorization: Parent approved second group after first-four runtime review.
image_processing: Original built-in image_gen output copied byte-for-byte. No creature pixel editing, recolouring, matting, alpha replacement or re-encoding.

observations: Seven slender grey-brown insects and a loose open-centre grouping clearly differ from the three large striped bee miniatures.
ANATOMY READABILITY FAILURE: most insects show only one obvious wing from this overhead view; one insect shows a clear pair. This does not establish consistent paired midge wings.
All insects and base remain inside the canvas; alpha inspection passes.
review.selection_reason: Parent authorized one targeted built-in ImageGen correction to give each of seven midges a clear attached pair of wings while retaining the arrangement.
remaining_limits: Rejected first candidate retained; do not select until paired-wing anatomy is corrected and reviewed.
